description: Building CHECKPOINT—an offline-capable, deep-space crew health and telemetry monitoring console for long-duration Mars transit. integrating real-time health indicators, NASA-STD-3001 compliance, and clinical decision support to safeguard astronauts far from Earth. I am looking for passionate developers, UI/UX designers, and data/AI enthusiasts to collaborate with me at Athlone for the NASA Space Apps Challenge!
summary:
CHECKPOINT is an offline-first prototype designed to support crew awareness during medical and operational incidents on long-duration space missions, where communication with Earth may be delayed. It brings simulated crew vitals, radiation exposure, cabin conditions, alerts, incident coordination, tasks, and message queues into one mission-control interface. A data-quality panel highlights missing or stale readings, while guest mode lets users explore fictional emergency scenarios without creating an account.
By making uncertainty and communication delays visible, CHECKPOINT helps operators organize information and coordinate human review when timely support is limited. The project demonstrates how a crew could maintain a clearer picture of an evolving situation in isolation. It is a simulation, not a certified medical device, and is not intended for real patient or sensitive data.
details:
CHECKPOINT is a mission-control prototype designed to explore a dangerous challenge in space travel: how a crew might recognize and coordinate a response to health or environmental problems when communication with Earth is delayed.

The application brings simulated crew readings, radiation exposure, cabin conditions, alerts, incident checklists, medical supplies, mission logs, and messages into one console. A data-quality panel highlights missing or stale information, while an operations desk helps users track tasks and handovers. The Earth Link feature simulates communication delays and offline queues. Users can explore the full console without a password or optionally sign in to a separate local demo workspace.

We developed CHECKPOINT using React, TypeScript, Vite, Python, Flask, SQLite, CSS, and Three.js. Its interactive 3D mission visualization, animated interface, and body-view display make complex information more engaging and easier to navigate.

In designing the project, we considered delayed communications, limited connectivity, accessibility, data separation, and the need for human review. CHECKPOINT is a simulation, not a medical device: its data and guidance are fictional or unverified, and it should not be used for real medical decisions or sensitive information.
